traffic.name: Ox cart
traffic.note: Two oxen and a two-wheeled cart; the carter walks at the near ox with a goad.

traffic.name: Carrier's wagon
traffic.note: Goods under a canvas tilt, horses in file, the carrier on foot.

traffic.name: Pack train
traffic.note: Where the roads are bad, goods go on horseback in strings.

traffic.name: Rider
traffic.note: A merchant on a palfrey.

traffic.name: Wheelbarrow
traffic.note: For short hauls about the town.

traffic.name: Farm wagon
traffic.note: The ladder-sided farm wagon, a pair abreast, the farmer on the front board.

traffic.name: Stage coach
traffic.note: Four horses, a coachman on the box and a postilion on the near leader.

traffic.name: Town carriage
traffic.note: A rich family behind glass, a pair, the coachman in livery.

traffic.name: Sedan chair
traffic.note: For hire in every large town, carried by two chairmen.

traffic.name: Courier
traffic.note: The post and the army move news at the trot.

traffic.name: Supply wagon
traffic.note: Four horses, the driver riding the near wheeler.

traffic.name: Ox cart
traffic.note: The Anatolian cart on solid wheels, drawn by buffalo.

traffic.name: Covered araba
traffic.note: Families travel under a canopy behind oxen, at a walk.

traffic.name: Camel caravan
traffic.note: A string of camels led by a man on a donkey.

traffic.name: Pack donkey
traffic.note: Water, charcoal and vegetables reach the lanes on donkeys.

traffic.name: Mounted agha
traffic.note: A man of rank rides.

traffic.name: Kago
traffic.note: A basket slung from one pole on two bearers.

traffic.name: Norimono
traffic.note: The lacquered palanquin of samurai rank, on four bearers.

traffic.name: Daihachiguruma
traffic.note: Edo had almost no wheeled carriages: goods move on big handcarts pulled by men.

traffic.name: Pack horse
traffic.note: Horses are led, not driven: a groom walks at the head.

traffic.name: Mounted samurai
traffic.note: Only samurai ride in town, with a spear-bearer and an attendant on foot behind.

traffic.name: Plaustrum
traffic.note: The ox cart on solid wheels; towns keep heavy carts off the streets by day.

traffic.name: Mule cart
traffic.note: A light cart behind two mules, the driver on the front board.

traffic.name: Carpentum
traffic.note: A covered two-wheeled carriage, the privilege of matrons and priests.

traffic.name: Litter
traffic.note: By day the rich cross town on the shoulders of four bearers.

traffic.name: Pack mules
traffic.note: Oil, wine and grain in panniers, a muleteer at the head.

traffic.name: Messenger
traffic.note: A rider without stirrups.

traffic.name: Motor car
traffic.note: Still rare: a doctor, a mayor, an officer.

traffic.name: Lorry
traffic.note: Army and haulage lorries under canvas, often in convoy.

traffic.name: Horse cart
traffic.note: Most local haulage is still horse-drawn, now on rubber tyres.

traffic.name: Bicycle
traffic.note: The working town rides to its shift.

traffic.name: Tram
traffic.note: Electric trams shuttle along the main street.
